# Cammasāṭakajātaka (Ja 324)
**ID:** Ja 324
**Section:** Jātaka (ja)
**Collection:** Suttas-Late-1
**Title (Pali):** Cammasāṭakajātaka
**SuttaCentral:** https://suttacentral.net/ja324
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0513m.mul3.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Cammasāṭakajātaka* (Ja 324) is a story found within the Pali Jātaka collection [SuttaCentral]. The framing narrative relates that the Buddha delivered this teaching while residing at Jetavana, occasioned by a mendicant wanderer (*paribbājaka*) clad in a leather cloak or jerkin (*cammasāṭaka*) [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1883]. While wandering for alms in Sāvatthī, the leather-clad ascetic mistakenly mistook the aggressive retreat of a fighting ram (*eḷaka*) for a gesture of reverence and was struck down [Fausböll 1883]. The canonical verse narrative opens with the phrase *kalyāṇarūpo vatāyam* ("The kindly beast"), and concludes with the identification of the characters (*samodhāna*), in which the foolish wanderer is identified with his present counterpart, and the wise merchant who witnessed the event is revealed to have been the Bodhisatta [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1883].
In addition to its literary transmission, the *Cammasāṭakajātaka* is attested in ancient Buddhist visual art at Bharhut, where it appears on the inner face of the stupa coping [Wood 2005]. Unlike the majority of Bharhut coping jātakas that are confined to a single swag of the sculpted vine, this narrative occupies two consecutive loops separated by ornamental swags, demonstrating a multi-scene visual depiction [Wood 2005]. Furthermore, despite lacking an inscribed title (*titulus*), the narrative remains identifiable through its distinctive visual elements [Wood 2005].
According to machine-calculated analysis by DharmaNexus, the text shares six matching segments with the third volume of the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* (S0513a3), with the longest parallel spanning verses §3.1–3.4 [DharmaNexus]. No cross-language matches with Chinese, Tibetan, or Sanskrit corpora meet the matching threshold [DharmaNexus], and SuttaCentral does not record curated cross-language parallels [SuttaCentral].
**Parallels and text reuse**

- Text reuse within the Pali corpus (DharmaNexus): Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā (Tatiyo bhāgo) (Atk S0513a3) (§3.1–3.4 ↔ §637–638)
